Martial Artist.name: Martial Artist
Martial Artist.description:
🥋 You control a fight with throws, joint locks, pins and precise strikes, redirecting force instead of overpowering it.

🌱 Built on long practice in judo, aikido, karate, jujutsu or a family school. Works with any Quirk or none.
🎯 You can end a fight without lasting harm, and agencies value clean, nonlethal captures.
⚠️ Much larger or armored opponents, and Quirks that keep you at range, limit what leverage can do.
📈 You learn more techniques as your Grappling and Striking improve.
⚖️ Restraining someone is legal in self-defense or to stop a crime, then you hand them to the police. Injuring with a lock beyond that is assault.

📈 Grants: Technique +1, Grappling +15, Striking +10
⚡ Starting technique: Borrowed Force Throw
Martial Artist.traitNarrativeEffects: Formal unarmed martial art: balance, timing, leverage; throws people who rush them, locks joints, pins, lands exact strikes on nerves and soft targets. At start they subdue an untrained adult without injury and hold their own against a trained fighter of similar build; much larger or stronger foes, armored or hardened bodies, or Quirks that keep them at range limit leverage. Not covered: weapons, ranged attacks, binding a captive (Capture). Pure training: the same if Quirkless; techniques cost stamina, never Quirk Strain. Legal and social treatment: restraint is legal in self-defense or to stop a crime in progress, then the person goes to the police; injuring with a lock beyond that is assault. Martial arts are respected; many police and heroes train. Agencies value clean, nonlethal captures; a villain trained this way is rarer and more dangerous. How it looks: balanced stance, open hands, quiet footwork, a bow before bouts, worn training clothes or school belt.
